checks.finding: T-007 is Risk: high, but its Scope and Planned Files are limited to test/CI registration, acceptance mapping, and user documentation; it explicitly excludes installer and core reimplementation. The risk-classification policy assigns docs and test-only changes to low, and the reviewer check treats high/critical classification of test-only work as a Major defect.

T-001–T-007 are high or critical and use Required Workflow: tdd. Their Done When sections call for Red→Green evidence, but none requires the failing test to be committed before implementation begins. Their Done When sections also request an independent review verdict without requiring a named second reviewer distinct from the implementer. T-005 does separately require a signed bundle and a distinct named second approver; that does not identify the independent reviewer.

T-004 combines separate Claude and Codex adapter normalization, final-output capture, transcript reconciliation, manual and automatic compaction handling, resume, and native timeout/barrier evidence. This spans more than three implementation areas for one focused task.

Functional task criteria have associated planned error or edge-path coverage: for example, T-001 maps to AC-014/016, T-002 to AC-003/008/015/017, T-003 to AC-005/006/018, and T-004 to AC-004/009/010/012/015.
No separate test-only task declares a test type that conflicts with its scope.
Every high/critical task includes a Rollback field addressing disabling or reverting the owned change while preserving required safety controls.
Potential installer/build overlap is sequenced: T-006 is blocked by T-004 and T-005, and global constraints require shared installer/build/CI edits to be serialized.
Blockers reflect the implementation sequence: T-002 follows T-001; T-003 follows T-002; T-004/T-005 follow T-003; T-006 follows both; and T-007 follows T-006.
SKIP: no bugfix or debugging task in scope.

findings.finding: T-007 is classified high although its scope is test/CI registration, acceptance mapping, and documentation, with no installer or core implementation. Under risk-classification-policy.md and the RISK-APPROPRIATE rule, test-only/documentation work is low risk; the current tier overstates its scope.

For T-001–T-007, Done When does not require a failing TDD test to be committed before implementation or identify a named independent reviewer distinct from the implementer. T-005 names a distinct second approver and requires a signed bundle, but does not satisfy the separate named-independent-reviewer requirement.

T-004 combines two host adapters with event normalization, final-output capture, transcript reconciliation, manual/automatic compact behavior, resume, and native timeout/barrier verification. These are more than three distinct implementation areas for one focused task.
